newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-Feb oil imports up 63 pct on 1996.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-Feb oil imports up 63 pct on 1996.

text.p: Brazilian imports of fuels and lubricants soared in early 1997 because of increased demand and higher international prices, said Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, Economic Policy Secretary at the Finance Ministry.

The Finance Ministry said Wednesday in its monthly report on the economy that up to February 23, average daily oil and lubricant imports stood at $30.53 million against a daily average of $18.68 million in the same period a year ago.
Mendonca de Barros told reporters this was the result of greater internal demand, which he said was up 5.0 percent, and higher international prices, up 20 percent.
Mendonca de Barros also noted January 1996 was a low comparative base in terms of economic activity.
Brazil posted a $1.621 billion trade deficit for the year to February 23. Average daily exports so far were at $170 million while average daily imports hit $216 million.

Among imports that showed significant year-on-year gains were passenger cars with a 199.9 percent increase to $6.0 million a day. Iron and steel products rose 92.9 percent to $4.65 million a day and other metal products rose 116.4 percent to average $2.36 million a day.
